rationale: hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=False, epochs=14, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=FRESH search-20260619-01 iter-1 FEASIBILITY (corrected protocol: val=ALL 214 L277 slices + 321px detector-geometry FOV; HARD 20-min train+score budget; staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, per-sample-ps FBP init + per-step model.projector swap, bg_target=truth, no fov= override). Hammernik-VN = MRI variational net ported to CT: T untied unrolled steps, each = learned filter-bank + per-filter RBF activation (the _rho_prime bump loop) PLUS an in-loop PYRO-NN projector data-consistency step (architectural twin of LPD/ItNet but tiny interpretable regulariser). CRITICAL LESSON from the SIBLING hammernik_2017 iter-1: it did NOT diverge to 0.0 -- it CUDA-OOM'd in _rho_prime at 72s with batch_size=4 (16GB RTX5000; the (B,F,H,W)=(4,16,512,512) x 31-bump RBF tensors + 5-step autograd blew the card). So the dominant iter-1 risk here is MEMORY, not divergence. MITIGATION: batch_size=2 (NOT 4), vn_n_filters=16 (below the 24 default -> fewer RBF tensors), vn_checkpoint=true (gradient-checkpoints each unrolled step -- hammernik_vn HAS this knob, cuts activation memory ~T-fold; this is the key difference that lets the projector-in-loop VN fit where the 2017 batch=4 did not). STABILITY against the documented VN family divergence/NaN->0.0 trap: grad_clip=1.0 (MANDATORY -- the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward; clip_and_step also SKIPS nonfinite-gradient batches so a poisoned step can't collapse the recon to a constant), vn_dc_norm=true (power-iter normalizes R^T(Rx-g) so softplus(lambda_t) stays O(1) regardless of geometry -- the safeguard the projector-less 2017 lacked), lr=5e-4 (the documented hammernik_vn optimum from the discarded run; 8e-4 was worse, brief caps lr<=5e-4), vn_lambda_init=2.3e-3 (loose VN-port working-corner hint). CAPACITY conservative per brief: vn_T=5, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0 (FBP recon is ~O(1) so the RBF grid [-1,1] covers it). BUDGET: reference -- LPD (projector-in-loop, T=7, ep30, train200, score214) ran 1150s/19.2min right at the edge; hammernik_vn at T=5/N_k=16/checkpointed should be comparable-or-cheaper per step. max_train_s=1000 (16.7min in-solver wall) is the BINDING constraint (epochs=14 is just an upper bound the wall trips first), leaving ~3min for score(214)+figure under the 30min SLURM kill. HYPOTHESIS: if I run a budget-sized, MEMORY-SAFE (batch=2, checkpointed), STABLE (grad_clip=1.0, dc_norm) Hammernik-VN, I expect (a) it AVOIDS the hammernik_2017 OOM and produces a FINITE val_ssim within 20min, and (b) the projector DC step lands it near or above the ~0.84 LD-FBP SSIM floor -- because a learned-regulariser + true-projector-DC unroll is a sound Mayo recon family (sibling LPD/ItNet/DD-sup all run finite here). This onboarding iter establishes the corrected-metric VN baseline that iter-2+ tunes one knob at a time (epochs/wall first to confirm convergence, then vn_T or vn_lambda_init).

hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=24, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.0023, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=False, epochs=10, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=hammernik_vn iter-2 (search-20260619-01). ONE KNOB: vn_n_filters 16->24 (all else held: vn_T=5, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, lr=5e-4, batch_size=2, vn_checkpoint=true, grad_clip=1.0, vn_dc_norm=true, vn_lambda_init=2.3e-3, max_train_s=1000, train_n=200, val_n=214, seed=42). DIAGNOSIS from iter-1 SLURM log (765196): training CONVERGED by epoch 3 (loss 5.2e-6 ep3 -> 1.6e-6 ep7, asymptotically flat; wall tripped at ep7/14 in 1000s), and the VN settled at SSIM 0.805 BELOW its own FBP init (baseline SSIM ~0.84, baseline_PSNR 34.08). This is a CONVERGED-BUT-BAD basin, NOT under-training -- so epochs-up is INERT here (the proven epochs lever applied to genuinely under-trained trainers; this one has flat loss). lambda_t never moved from init (0.0023 across all 5 steps), so the tiny-DC + 16-filter regulariser converged to a BLUNT SMOOTHER that degrades the FBP init below baseline. Per the brief conditional (epochs-up if budget allows, ELSE vn_n_filters or lr): training is converged AND near the wall -> capacity knob. vn_n_filters 16->24 (the solver default capacity) gives the learned filter bank enough degrees of freedom to learn an EDGE-PRESERVING regulariser instead of the smoothing it collapsed to with 16 filters. NOT touching lr (campaign has lr5e-4-optimal / 8e-4-worse on record). HYPOTHESIS: with 24 filters the regulariser can preserve structure rather than smooth, lifting val_ssim ABOVE the iter-1 0.805 and ideally to/above the ~0.84 FBP floor (hr>0). FALSIFIER: if val_ssim stays <=0.81 (still <FBP), the VN family is structurally smoothing-bound at this DC weight regardless of filter count, and iter-3 must instead raise the DC weight (vn_lambda_init) so data-consistency dominates the regulariser. BUDGET: 24 filters ~1.3x the per-step RBF/conv cost; iter-1 did 7 ep in 1000s (143 s/ep) so expect ~5 ep in the 1000s wall -- still >3 (convergence point), so the converged-comparison is fair. Memory safe: vn_checkpoint=true + batch_size=2 keep N_k=24 (the solver memory-fitted default) within the card. max_train_s=1000 unchanged; total ~1300s under the 1800s SLURM kill.

column13: hammernik_vn-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=24, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=1.0, vn_lambda_init=0.05, vn_init=fbp, vn_dc_norm=True, vn_checkpoint=True, vn_normalize_filters=False, epochs=10, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=200, val_n=214, max_train_s=1000, seed=42, rationale=hammernik_vn iter-3 (search-20260619-01, corrected 214-slice/321px-FOV metric). ONE KNOB: vn_lambda_init 0.0023 -> 0.05 (~22x DC-weight init). All else held at iter-2 (vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=24, vn_kernel=11, vn_n_bumps=31, lr=5e-4, batch_size=2, vn_checkpoint=true, grad_clip=1.0, vn_dc_norm=true, vn_init=fbp, max_train_s=1000, train_n=200, val_n=214, seed=42). PRIOR (NUMBERS): iter-1 SSIM 0.80528 (vn_n_filters=16, hr=0, elapsed 1295.7s); iter-2 SSIM 0.79195 (vn_n_filters=24, hr=0, elapsed 1351.7s, train 1191.6s). The iter-2 filter bump 16->24 did NOT help -- it REGRESSED -0.0133 (0.80528->0.79195). Both sit BELOW the LD-FBP floor (baseline SSIM ~0.84, baseline_PSNR=34.08), so hr=0. This FIRES iter-2's own pre-registered falsifier ('if val_ssim stays <=0.81 still <FBP, the VN is smoothing-bound regardless of filter count, iter-3 must raise the DC weight vn_lambda_init'). DIAGNOSIS from iter-2 SLURM log 765279: dc_norm power-iter ~= 1.47e+03; training CONVERGED (loss 4.9e-4 ep1 -> 1.3e-6 ep6, flat by ep3) -- NOT under-training, so epochs-up is INERT; and CRITICALLY lambda_t stayed pinned at ['0.0023','0.00231','0.00231','0.00231','0.00231'] across ALL epochs -- Adam never grew the learnable DC weight from its init. The update is u <- u - KT_rho - lam * R^T(Ru-g)/dc_norm (solver lines 141-156): with lam ~= 0.0023 the data-consistency pull is negligible vs the learned regulariser gradient KT_rho, so the VN converges to a blunt smoother that degrades the FBP init below baseline. LIMITER = DC weight too small (NOT capacity: filters^ regressed; NOT epochs: loss flat). Since lambda_t never moves from init, the init vn_lambda_init IS the lever. vn_lambda_init 0.0023 -> 0.05 makes data-consistency dominate the regulariser from step 1 so the recon stays anchored to the measured sinogram instead of over-smoothing. lr held (campaign has lr5e-4-optimal / 8e-4-worse on record). HYPOTHESIS: with the DC init ~22x stronger, val_ssim clears the FBP floor (val_ssim > 0.84, hr>0). FALSIFIER: if val_ssim stays <=0.84 (still <FBP), the VN regulariser is structurally degrading even under strong DC, and iter-4 must attack the regulariser itself (vn_normalize_filters=True to constrain filters zero-mean/unit-norm, or vn_init=backproj). BUDGET (HARD 20-min train+score; sbatch --time=00:30:00): the lambda VALUE does not change per-step compute (same forward/back-project DC step), so cost ~= iter-2: train 1191.6s (max_train_s=1000 binds, ~6 epochs) + ~160s score(214)+figure = ~1352s, under the 1800s SLURM kill. MEMORY-SAFE: identical footprint to iter-2 -- batch_size=2 + vn_checkpoint=true keep N_k=24 within the 16 GB card (no OOM; cf. the hammernik_2017 bs=4 OOM). grad_clip=1.0 retained (VN-family NaN-skip stability; the 2304-view Mayo FBP adjoint overflows the backward otherwise -- and a stronger DC step makes the clip MORE load-bearing).
